subject.title: fix: show readable session names across Windows UX

question: Should ordinary Windows session surfaces hide every Gateway-classified background session by default, with only an explicit Sessions-page toggle and active-chat exception exposing them?
rationale: This changes established visibility across multiple user surfaces; tests can prove consistency but cannot determine whether hiding cron, heartbeat, subagent, ACP, hook, harness, and other background families is the intended product policy.

options.title: Hide By Default
options.body: Approve the proposed foreground-first behavior, retaining the explicit background toggle and active-session exception.

options.title: Preserve Visibility
options.body: Land friendly titles and structured grouping while continuing to show existing sessions by default until filtering is designed separately.

options.title: Narrow The Scope
options.body: Limit this PR to additive metadata parsing and readable naming, moving all visibility changes to a focused follow-up.

recommendation.title: Hide By Default
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed foreground-first behavior, retaining the explicit background toggle and active-session exception.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the paired issue and coordinated both sides of the proposed presentation contract, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the policy decision.
